summary.intent: Build a full interactive TUI dashboard for the memory-loop feature using Charmbracelet/bubbletea libraries, covering all 12 subcommands in a single tabbed interface.
summary.outcome: A complete `memorylooptui` package was designed and implemented with 4 tabs (Memories, Injection, History, Settings), full lifecycle management keybindings, an inline add-memory form, and a prompt tester. All lint/tests passed and changes were committed across multiple commits.

repo: Existing CLI uses a `termstyle` package for ANSI 256-color styling with NO_COLOR support — TUI must follow this palette rather than defining its own.
Memory loop functionality lives in `cmd/entire/cli/memoryloop/memoryloop.go` with functions: TransitionRecordLifecycle, SelectRelevant, AddManualRecord, PruneRecords, SaveState.
The project uses `ACCESSIBLE=1` env var pattern (via huh forms) — bubbletea TUIs should fall back to plain-text subcommands when this is set.
Package structure follows feature-based directories: `memoryloop/`, `insights/`, `settings/` — new TUI package named `memorylooptui/` is consistent.
go.mod lint errors on uncommitted go.mod changes are expected/benign in this repo's CI flow.

code.finding: Keyboard shortcuts designed to be mnemonic: a=activate, s=suppress, u=unsuppress, x=archive (avoids conflict with 'a'), P=promote (uppercase avoids conflict with policy toggle 'p').
Root model wires cobra command entry point and holds composite state for all 4 tab sub-models.
Most complex tab: table + status filter bar + expandable detail pane + lifecycle actions all in one model.
Shared rendering helpers: tab bar, status bar, strength bar (5-block ████░ format), time formatting — extracted to avoid duplication across tab files.

workflow: Brainstorming skill + visual companion server (localhost) was used to present HTML mockups of layout options and get user approval before writing specs — effective for visual/UI design decisions.
Tasks 1-3 were batched into a single implementer dispatch since they were tightly coupled foundational scaffolding with no independent value.
Subagent-driven development pattern: implementer → spec reviewer (skipped for scaffold) → code reviewer → fix subagent → final commit worked well.
Fix subagent committed its own changes before the orchestrator checked — orchestrator must verify recent commits before assuming what's uncommitted.
Code reviewer findings were triaged: real bugs fixed immediately, tests and async spinner wired deferred to open items.

friction: Fix subagent committed changes independently, causing the orchestrator to incorrectly assume those files still had uncommitted changes — required an extra git log check to reconcile state.
Tasks 5-8 tab implementations were not committed by their implementer agents, requiring a manual catch-up commit at the end.
gomod lint errors on uncommitted go.mod added noise to lint output during development, requiring a knowledge check to confirm benign.
open_items: Unit tests for TUI components are absent — design spec flagged 'manual verification' focus; test coverage deferred.
Async refresh spinner in History tab is not wired to a real background command — spinner UI exists but refresh trigger is a stub.
Prune action was added to keybindings during spec self-review but implementation completeness should be verified.
Accessible mode fallback (ACCESSIBLE=1 → plain-text subcommands) is specified in the design but not yet implemented in the cobra command entry point.
